result:
I keep a small stone in my pocket from the river behind my grandmother's house. It's smooth and warm from being held, and I don't know why I still carry it. Maybe because some things are easier to keep than people.

Evenings are getting longer now. The light slants through the kitchen blinds in thin gold bars, and the cats move through them like they understand something about time I don't. I make tea I don't drink. I read the same page three times.

I think a lot about the word 'enough'. Not as a finish line, but as a softening. Enough light, enough money, enough love. We spend so much time chasing more, and then one day we realize more was never the point. The point was the table, the conversation, the way someone laughs when they think no one is listening.

I met a man on the bus last winter who told me he talks to the plants in his apartment. He named them after old jazz musicians. I wanted to tell him I talk to mine too, but I didn't. I just nodded.

If I could write a letter to myself at twenty, I wouldn't give advice. I'd just say: you will be okay, and you will be lonely sometimes, and both can be true. Bring a sweater. Call your mother back.

The stone is still in my pocket. It doesn't do anything. That's why I like it.
